subject: barnstormerBiplane
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: barnstormer biplane.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, the biplane's identity cues read well—wings, struts, prop, radial engine—but the pilot and bear passenger are barely visible, mostly hidden behind the wing, windscreen, and cabane struts, while the bunting and checkered tips add nice whimsy. The main issue to fix is making the pilot and bear more visible rather than tucked out of sight.

I'm considering raising the upper wing's y-position and adjusting the cabane struts to free up space for the characters, but that cascades into many other coordinates tied to the wing height—fuel tank, nav light, decal, bunting all reference that same value. Rather than editing each occurrence individually, I'm thinking of introducing a single constant for the upper wing's y-position and replacing all the scattered references to it consistently.

I'm also realizing the bear character gets hidden under the wing and behind the windscreen in both top and side views, which isn't ideal. Since real biplanes often have a cutout in the upper wing's center section, I'm considering modifying the wing outline polygon to add a notch there so the character underneath becomes visible.

Checking the geometry, the bear sits near z=0.3 but the notch only reaches z~0.3, so they overlap -- I need to deepen the notch or reposition the bear so the clearance actually works out in the mapped coordinates.

Let me check if the cabane struts might collide with the bear's body given their x and z positions — I may need to shift the bear back slightly to keep clearance from both the pilot cockpit and the strut geometry.

Simplifying with specific rod coordinates for the rear and front cabane struts, plus a wire connecting the cabane top to the lower wing. I'm also bumping up the pilot's head radius and adjusting the face decal sizing to match.

Scaling the pilot head means touching many helmet-related offset values scattered across the module, which is risky given how large a full rewrite would be -- I'll stick to targeted edits instead. Separately, I need to reposition the bunting since it's currently blocking the characters in the front view; better to hang it along the lower side of the upper wing between the outer struts on each side.

Computing the swag curve coordinates...

Checking the prop and fuselage next, then noticing the sign's position overlaps the crate and drums in the front view — I'm weighing whether to reposition it, but the base being large relative to the plane makes it a minor issue worth leaving as is.

Now I'm checking pilot visibility: the pilot's head sits above the bear's head and both should now clear the wing after raising it, giving good separation in the front view once the heads are sized up a bit.

I'll settle on raising the wing to 3.25 for a more balanced gap-to-chord ratio, and bump up both the pilot's and bear's head sizes slightly for visibility. I'm also considering whether the pilot's face details, like a moustache, would even be noticeable in a top-down view.

The helmet, earflaps, and goggles are all tied to specific radius values, so enlarging the head isn't as simple as changing one number — I'll need to adjust several related measurements together or just leave the head size alone.

Still scaling head feature coordinates...

Adjusting proportions for the bear head and nose placement...

Adjusting bear body height for proper head overlap, and checking the pilot's waving arm position and the top-wing decal placement relative to the tank and notch.

Checking that the notch depth and corner smoothing won't cause edge-crossing errors in the extrude outline — the vertical and horizontal segments are long enough that quarter-length corner cuts stay well clear of neighboring edges.

I'm adding an optional `notch` parameter to `wingOutline` so only the upper wing gets the cut, splicing in the four extra notch points between the existing left/right outline points while keeping the winding order consistent.

I need to define UY alongside the existing grass base constant, then update the strut y-coordinate to reference UY instead of the old literal value. I'm checking the aileron and rod/wire connections to confirm they already use these variables correctly without conflicting with the wing notch.

Writing cabane strut rods...

Checking the overlap between the pilot's screen at -0.4 and the bear cockpit's rear rim near -0.30 — close but acceptable given the pilot's windscreen is short. Adjusting the bear's z-position to 0.05 keeps its screen and goggles placement consistent at the new offset.

Now I'm tracing every other spot that references 3.0 as a y-coordinate — the wing definition, the emblem decal position, the tank sphere and cap cylinder, and the nav light glow — all of which need updating to the new UY value.

I also need to find and replace the bunting block exactly, which builds a sagging catmull-rom path across the fuselage and sweeps a thin wire along it, then groups decorative elements along that path.

Rewriting bunting path logic...

I'm double-checking the wing's vertical positioning so the flags hang correctly and the leading edge sits just in front of the rounded wing tip.

The front struts and bunting sit at separate z-depths so they won't clash, and there's no front prop to worry about. The sign and bunting overlap seem fine to leave, though the base looks oversized relative to the model's dimensions—something to keep in mind.

Checking visibility: the lower wing light position looks right, rudder is fine, and the lower wing appropriately hides the lower fuselage in front view. For faces, the bear and pilot positions work after enlarging, but I'm noticing the spinning prop blade might overlay the cockpit region where the bear's head is—I should rotate the prop blades to avoid that visual conflict.

Adjusting prop blade angle...

Now I'm planning the edits as a numbered list, making sure each search snippet (like the grass base constant and wing outline coordinates) is unique before applying changes.

Checking the decal placement line, the wing extrude call, and the tank's repositioned coordinates for uniqueness so each targeted edit matches exactly one spot.

Still writing pilot head details...

I'm checking the goggle placement geometry against the helmet dome coverage—verifying the normalized direction vector puts the goggle elevation within the helmet's lower edge boundary so it doesn't poke out above the dome.

Satisfied goggles sit correctly on the helmet, so I'm now setting up a bear figure with a spherical head, bear-face decal, and a small ink dot detail.

Adding ears and windscreen placement...
